ajanta-caves.blurb: 30 rock-cut Buddhist caves in a horseshoe gorge, carved between the 2nd century BCE and 6th century CE, famous for painted murals of the Jataka tales.

ellora-caves.blurb: 34 caves cut side by side — Buddhist, Hindu and Jain — crowned by the Kailasa Temple, carved top-down from a single basalt cliff.

agra-fort.blurb: Mughal red-sandstone fortress on the Yamuna, built by Akbar and later the site of Shah Jahan's confinement, with a clear view of the Taj.

taj-mahal.blurb: Shah Jahan's white-marble mausoleum for Mumtaz Mahal, finished in 1653 and inlaid with semi-precious stone — best seen at sunrise, before the crowds.

konark-sun-temple.blurb: A 13th-century temple built as a colossal stone chariot for the sun god, its wheels carved as working sundials, half-ruined but still monumental.

mahabalipuram-monuments.blurb: Pallava-era rock-cut shrines and the Shore Temple facing the Bay of Bengal, alongside the giant open-air relief known as Arjuna's Penance.

kaziranga-national-park.blurb: Assam grassland and swampland reserve holding the world's largest population of one-horned rhinoceros, best explored by jeep or elephant-back safari.

manas-wildlife-sanctuary.blurb: Foothill forest on the Bhutan border sheltering tigers, elephants and the rare golden langur — quieter and far less visited than Kaziranga.

keoladeo-national-park.blurb: A former royal duck-hunting marsh near Bharatpur, now a wetland sanctuary drawing thousands of migratory birds every winter.

goa-churches-convents.blurb: 16th–17th century Portuguese churches in Old Goa, including the Basilica of Bom Jesus, which holds the relics of St. Francis Xavier.

khajuraho-monuments.blurb: Chandela-dynasty temples from the 10th–11th centuries, celebrated for intricately carved sculpture — only a fraction of the original 85 temples survive.

hampi-monuments.blurb: The boulder-strewn ruins of Vijayanagara's capital — temples, bazaars and a stone chariot spread across a landscape that looks otherworldly at dawn.

fatehpur-sikri.blurb: Akbar's short-lived red-sandstone capital, abandoned within 15 years for lack of water — its palaces and the towering Buland Darwaza remain intact.

pattadakal-monuments.blurb: A cluster of 7th–8th century Chalukya temples blending northern and southern Indian temple styles side by side on the Malaprabha river.

elephanta-caves.blurb: A short ferry ride from Mumbai's Gateway of India to rock-cut Shiva shrines, centred on a monumental three-faced Sadashiva sculpture.

chola-temples.blurb: Three living Shiva temples built over three centuries by Chola kings, headlined by the towering 11th-century Brihadeeswarar Temple at Thanjavur.

sundarbans-national-park.blurb: The world's largest mangrove forest, shared with Bangladesh, explored by boat through tidal channels where the Bengal tiger still swims between islands.

nanda-devi-valley-of-flowers.blurb: A high-Himalayan wilderness of alpine meadows and snow peaks around Nanda Devi, open to trekkers only through the short monsoon bloom.

sanchi-buddhist-monuments.blurb: India's best-preserved Buddhist stupa complex, founded by Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE, with elaborately carved gateways added later by the Sungas.

humayuns-tomb.blurb: A garden tomb built for the Mughal emperor Humayun in the 1560s, and the direct architectural template for the Taj Mahal decades later.

qutb-minar.blurb: A 73-metre tapering minaret begun in 1193 to mark the start of Delhi's Sultanate era, standing beside an even older iron pillar.

mountain-railways-india.blurb: Three narrow-gauge Himalayan lines — Darjeeling, Nilgiri and Kalka–Shimla — still climbing steep grades on steam and diesel toy trains.

mahabodhi-temple-bodhgaya.blurb: The site where the Buddha is believed to have attained enlightenment, under a descendant of the original Bodhi tree — still an active pilgrimage site.

bhimbetka-rock-shelters.blurb: Sandstone rock shelters with paintings spanning the Mesolithic to medieval periods — among the earliest evidence of human life in India.

chhatrapati-shivaji-terminus.blurb: A Victorian Gothic railway station in daily use, its spires and turrets modelled on London's St Pancras and still Mumbai's busiest terminus.

champaner-pavagadh.blurb: An abandoned 16th-century sultanate capital at the foot of Pavagadh hill, blending Hindu and Islamic architecture across mosques, tombs and stepwells.

red-fort.blurb: Shah Jahan's red-sandstone citadel and seat of Mughal power for two centuries — every Independence Day, the Prime Minister addresses the nation from its ramparts.

jantar-mantar-jaipur.blurb: An 18th-century open-air observatory of stone astronomical instruments built by Maharaja Jai Singh II, including the world's largest stone sundial.

western-ghats.blurb: A mountain range older than the Himalayas, running down India's west coast — one of the world's biodiversity hotspots across 39 protected pockets.

hill-forts-rajasthan.blurb: Six hilltop Rajput forts, including Chittorgarh and Kumbhalgarh, built between the 5th and 18th centuries to guard the kingdoms below.

rani-ki-vav.blurb: An 11th-century stepwell built as a memorial by a Solanki queen, its seven descending levels carved with over 500 sculptures.

great-himalayan-national-park.blurb: A steep Himachal wilderness of conifer forest and alpine pasture, home to snow leopards and blue sheep, reached mainly on foot.

nalanda-mahavihara.blurb: Ruins of the ancient world's largest residential university, teaching Buddhist philosophy to students from across Asia from the 5th to 12th centuries.

khangchendzonga-national-park.blurb: A Sikkim reserve wrapped around the world's third-highest peak, sacred to local communities and home to red pandas and snow leopards.

le-corbusier-chandigarh.blurb: The Capitol Complex — Chandigarh's Secretariat, Assembly and High Court — designed by Le Corbusier as the centrepiece of India's first planned city.

historic-city-ahmadabad.blurb: A 15th-century walled city of carved-wood havelis and stepped pols, founded by Sultan Ahmad Shah on the banks of the Sabarmati.

victorian-gothic-artdeco-mumbai.blurb: Two adjoining South Mumbai precincts — Gothic Revival civic buildings around Oval Maidan facing an Art Deco skyline along Marine Drive.

jaipur-city.blurb: Rajasthan's pink-washed walled capital, planned in 1727 on a precise grid of nine blocks around the City Palace and Hawa Mahal.

ramappa-temple.blurb: A 13th-century Kakatiya temple with a roof said to be light enough to float on water, and sandstone carving famed for its detail.

dholavira.blurb: A 5,000-year-old Indus Valley city in the Rann of Kutch, with stone reservoirs and a stadium-sized ceremonial ground still visible today.

santiniketan.blurb: The university town Rabindranath Tagore built around open-air classrooms and rural craft, still run on the Visva-Bharati philosophy he founded in 1921.

hoysala-temples.blurb: Star-shaped 12th–13th century temples at Belur, Halebidu and Somanathapura, carved by Hoysala sculptors in soapstone fine enough to resemble ivory.

moidams-ahom.blurb: Earthen burial mounds of the Ahom dynasty at Charaideo, raised over six centuries and sometimes called Assam's own pyramids.

maratha-military-landscapes.blurb: Twelve hill, forest and coastal forts built by the Maratha empire, headlined by Shivaji's mountain stronghold at Raigad.

sarnath.blurb: The deer park where the Buddha gave his first sermon after enlightenment, marked today by the Ashoka pillar and the great Dhamek Stupa.
